title: What is known about 1RB1RA_0LC0RA_1LF0LD_1LE0RC_1LB1LD_1RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_0LC0RA_1LF0LD_1LE0RC_1LB1LD_1RB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The mechanism is now known and partly proved. The head sweeps right in state A (every 0 moves one cell right) and left two cells at a time in states E and D: a pair of cells 01 becomes 11, a pair 11 becomes 10. On a tape of blocks of ones of odd length this only moves the content two cells to the right per round trip; the right end eats it and the left end adds a new word 1 3 1 5 5 (block lengths) every six round trips. Everything else comes from defects, places where the left sweep lands on a 0: the head turns round there and bounces between the defect and the right end, which rebuilds the tape to the right of the defect in a longer pattern.

Lean proves (kernel) that a halt can only come from one pattern, state E on a 0 with 1 0 0 to its left, and that the machine never halts if that pattern never appears. The C simulator sees no halt in 6.1·1010 steps, and the pattern never: in that run E met two 0s in a row inside the tape 285 times, after step 3.6·107 always in the same harmless surrounding. 3,600 real tapes with one or two cells changed do not halt either, but small tapes of blocks do (111011 halts after 655 steps), so the shape of the tape alone does not prevent a halt. No closed set of configurations was found: the tape is nested to unbounded depth, so the closed-set method that found closed sets for two sibling machines does not apply as it stands, and four automatic searches for a regular invariant failed.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 18,938 cells have been visited and 14,202 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.405). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.479).

claims.title: The sweep rules and the single events
claims.text: 17 rules, for every repeat count and any tape around. Sweeps: A going right moves every 0 one cell right, D going left rewrites pairs, over the words 1101, 110111, 11, the 20-cell word of the left zone (blocks 1 3 1 5 5) and the 60-cell word of the second zone (blocks 3 1 3 1 3 5 5 3 5 5 3 1 3 1 3). Events: a single 0 moving right, the head stepping over two 0s, the right turn at three 0s, and the five cases of the left sweep landing on a 0 (e_bounce, e_z2_pass, e_z2_bounce, e_end, e_prehalt).

claims.title: Resets of the left zone
claims.text: The word 1 3 1 5 5 is added at the left end once per six round trips; at a reset the zone is rebuilt as copies of the 15-block word 3 1 3 1 3 5 5 3 5 5 3 1 3 1 3 (7, 33, 66, 65, 254 copies at the resets up to 109 steps). Resets (tape starts 1 00 11 when E steps off the left end) at steps 6,443; 52,596; 65,233; 1,072,500; 42,678,053; 106,638,874; 201,754,341; 921,618,056; 18,930,310,428; 61,568,762,133. No regular spacing; the last one ends a single stay of 7.4·109 steps away from the left end.

claims.title: The halt needs 1 C>0
claims.text: The only halting transition F1 is reached only from 1 C>0. In the first 109 steps C reads a 0 only 10,252 times, mostly at the ends of the tape. The kernel claim below sharpens this to one pattern three steps earlier.

claims.title: The regular left sweep, for any tape of pairs
claims.text: State E on the right cell of a pair, the pair being 01 or 11: after 2 or 4 steps the pair is 11 or 10 and E stands on the right cell of the next pair to the left. By induction the same holds for any list of such pairs, so on blocks of ones of odd length the left sweep is a fixed rewriting and never stops.

claims.title: A halt comes from exactly one pattern
claims.text: Three steps before any halt the machine is in state E on a 0 with 1 0 0 to its left (E0, B0, C0, then F reads the 1). So if the run from blank tape never shows 1 0 0 E>0, the machine never halts; and from that pattern it does halt.

claims.title: No halt in the first 6.1·10<sup>10</sup> steps, and the pattern never close
claims.text: Plain C simulation to step 61,568,762,133 (the tenth reset; 57,758 cells left of the start, 42,418 right). E read a 0 with another 0 on its left, inside the tape, 285 times; from step 3.6·107 on always as 0111 00 followed by 10, the case of rule e_z2_bounce, where the two 0s disappear. The halting surrounding 1 0 0 never occurred.

claims.title: Perturbed real tapes do not halt; small tapes of blocks do
claims.text: Tapes of the real run at three moments (3.8·106, 4.5·107, 2.3·108 steps) with one cell flipped, one cell deleted, a 0 or a 1 inserted, two cells flipped, or a 1 cleared next to a 0: 3,600 tapes, none halts within 2·106 steps. Tapes made of blocks of ones separated by single 0s are not safe in general: blocks 3, 2 (111011, state A on the first cell) halt after 655 steps, and of 2,000 random tapes of n blocks of lengths 1 to 5 those that halt within 3·106 steps number 62, 14, 0, 4, 2, 0, 1, 1 for n = 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 20, 30 (odd lengths 1, 3, 5, 7 only: 0, 29, 0, 3, 3, 0, 0, 0). Random bit strings halt often and early (they contain three 0s in a row). So, as for the two sibling machines, tapes of the same shape can halt; a proof has to use more of the real tape than its shape.

claims.title: Content drifts right; defects start inner bounces; the tape is nested
claims.text: Right sweep and regular left sweep together complement the pairs and shift them by one pair, so the content moves two cells right per round trip against a right end that stands still and consumes it. A defect (the left sweep landing on a 0: an even block or two 0s) is an inner left wall: the head bounces between it and the right end, the defect moves left one block per bounce, and what is to its right becomes new content with longer runs of blocks of 3. Defects nest, so at 109 steps the tape is a sequence of zones: (1 3 1 5 5)^a, the 15-block word 254 times, a 45-block word (the three words have 20, 60 and 180 cells), then runs (3)^k separated by a 1 or a 5 with k growing to the right. Composition of the proved rules, checked against traces; not formalised.

claims.title: No closed set found (four searches)
claims.text: (1) The closed-set method of the sibling machines needs a tape zone w^N T u^M tail with a bounded zone; here the number of zones grows, so there is no finite list of nodes. (2) Finite-automata reduction with a DFA that tracks parity and the last k ≤ 6 cells, on either side: the blank start is accepted as possibly halting. (3) A closed tape language whose states are windows of K runs (lengths exact up to a cap, then parity): K = 2, 3, 4 reach a halting abstract configuration, K = 5 exceeds 3·106 abstract configurations. Reason in both: a window forgets what lies beyond it, and windows from the left end get glued to inner ones (the real run visits 4,821 abstract configurations where the closure has 406,469). (4) The same with the far end of the tape, the number of even blocks and a parity added to the state: small sizes reach a halting abstract configuration, larger ones exceed 3·106 configurations; the abstraction cannot tell the long real tape from short block tapes, which do halt.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. What is missing is an invariant that excludes 1 0 0 E>0: two 0s in a row arise inside the tape only when the left sweep lands on the 0 after a block of length 1, and they are removed again by the next bounce unless a third 0 is adjacent. A proof has to control where the grid of pairs (fixed by the right end) stands relative to such places; a regular language with windows does not do it.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 6·10<sup>10</sup> steps without stopping. We now know exactly which pattern on the tape would stop it, and that pattern has never appeared; what is missing is a proof that it never will. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked with how it was checked.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; about 100,000 cells visited.
The only pattern a halt can come from, proved in Lean.
Real tapes with one or two cells changed that halt. Small tapes of blocks do halt.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.405). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.479).
After 109 steps the tape spans 18,938 cells (8,418 left of the start, 5,248 right), with a density of 1s of 0.75.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Content that drifts right, and zones of growing pattern
html:
Read the tape as lengths of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s. Almost all blocks have odd length: 1, 3, 5, sometimes 7. Next to the left end stands a zone of the word 1 3 1 5 5 repeated; then a zone of a 15-block word, a zone of a 45-block word (20, 60 and 180 cells: each word three times as long as the one before), and further right long runs of blocks of 3 separated by a single 1 or 5, the runs longer the further right. At 9.3·108 steps:

3 (1 3 1 5 5)^29 1 3 1 5 1 5 (3 3 1 3 1 3 5 5 3 5 5 3 1 3 1)^254 … (3)^8 5 (3)^12 5 (3)^7 1 … (3)^26 5 (3)^31 1

The head goes back and forth across the whole tape. One round trip moves all of this two cells to the right. The right end does not move: it swallows what arrives. The left end makes up for it: every three round trips it adds 4 cells, every six a new word 1 3 1 5 5. So the left zone grows steadily while the rest slides into the right end.

From time to time the head, on its way left, turns round in the middle of the tape, at a defect (next section). It then bounces between the defect and the right end, hundreds to billions of steps, and each bounce moves the defect one block to the left. What it leaves to the right of the defect is new content of the next kind: the word 1 3 1 5 5 three times becomes the 15-block word, that one becomes the 45-block word, and so on. A reset is a defect that travels all the way to the left end and rebuilds the whole left zone; resets came at steps 6,443; 52,596; 65,233; 1,072,500; 4.3·107; 1.1·108; 2.0·108; 9.2·108; 1.9·1010; 6.2·1010, with no regular spacing. Defects can sit inside the stretch of an earlier defect, so the zones are nested, and their number grows without bound.

sections.heading: Two cells at a time
html:
Going right the machine is in state A and does one thing: every 0 it meets moves one cell to the right. Three 0s in a row (the right end) turn it round.

Going left it alternates between states E and D and handles the tape in pairs of cells, E on the right cell, D on the left one:

pairbecomesthenLean
0111goes on to the next paire_pair, sweep
1110goes on to the next paire_pair, sweep
1001turns right: a bounce inside the tapee_bounce
01 0010 01goes one_z2_pass
11 0010 10turns righte_z2_bounce
00 0010 10turns right: the left end, 4 new cellse_end
10 00halts three steps latere_prehalt, prehalt

Example, blocks 5 5 before a left sweep, written with each 0 on the left cell of its pair: 01 11 11 | 01 11 11 becomes 11 10 10 | 11 10 10, the blocks 3 1 3 1 (the first 1s join the block on their left). The next right sweep moves each 0 one cell: the 0s are on left cells again. As long as every block has odd length, every 0 sits on a left cell and only the first two rows are used. A block of even length, or two 0s in a row, puts the following 0s on right cells: that is a defect, and the third row turns the head.

The first two rows are proved for any sequence of pairs (sweep), the rows as single rules, and the sweeps over the zone words for any number of copies (a_w0, d_w0, a_w1, d_w1 and five older rules), all checked by Lean's kernel.

sections.heading: Only from 1 0 0 0, met from the right
html: The machine has one halting transition: state F reading a 1. Lean proves that this can only happen in one way: the left sweep (state E) lands on a 0, the two cells to its left are 0 as well, and the cell before them is a 1. Three steps later F reads that 1. So: the machine halts if and only if a left sweep meets 1 0 0 0 with E on the last 0 (pre_of_halts, halts_of_1000, nonhalting_of_no_1000).

How close does the run come? Two 0s in a row inside the tape are rare. They arise when the left sweep lands on the 0 behind a block of length 1 (0 1 0 becomes 0 0 1, then the head bounces), and the next time the sweep comes by they are removed (row 11 00 of the table). In 6.1·1010 steps E stood on the second of two inner 0s 285 times; after step 3.6·107 the cells around were the same every time, 0 1 1 1 0 [0] 1 0. Inside the tape E never had two more 0s to its left.

Copies of real tapes with a cell flipped, removed or added never halted (3,600 tried). But the shape alone is not safe: the six-cell tape 111011 halts after 655 steps, and about 1 in 2,000 random tapes of 30 blocks halts. The real run avoids the halting pattern for a reason that is not yet understood.

Why is it still open? A proof needs a description of all tapes the run can reach that is closed under the machine's steps and excludes 1 0 0 0 in front of E. The tape is nested to unbounded depth, so a finite list of shapes with a few counters does not exist, and four automatic searches for a regular description (automata that remember a window of cells or of blocks) failed: whether a bounce is harmless depends on how the grid of pairs, which is fixed by the far right end, lies relative to the defect, and a window does not see that.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Bouncer whose left sweep rewrites the tape two cells at a time (01 to 11, 11 to 10): the content drifts right and is eaten at the right end, defects of parity start nested inner bounces; it halts only from 1 0 0 E>0, never seen in 6.1e10 steps.
family: bouncer with pair-rewriting sweep, drifting content and nested inner bounces

sections.heading: How it works
paragraphs: Going right (state A) every 0 moves one cell right. Going left (states E, D) the tape is rewritten in pairs of cells: 01 becomes 11, 11 becomes 10. On blocks of ones of odd length the two sweeps together only move the content two cells to the right; the right end consumes it, the left end adds the word 1 3 1 5 5 every six round trips.

When the left sweep lands on a 0 (an even block or two 0s: a defect) the head turns round inside the tape and bounces between the defect and the right end; the defect moves left and leaves a longer pattern behind. Defects nest, which gives zones of growing pattern and the irregular resets.

A halt needs the left sweep to land on the last 0 of 1 0 0 0 (proved in Lean). That never happened in 6.1·1010 steps, nor on 3,600 real tapes with a cell or two changed; small tapes of blocks do reach it, so the shape alone does not protect the run. A proof that it cannot happen is missing.
